bull.b: Persistent, high free cash flow (roughly $10B TTM) gives Uber durable financial flexibility to fund strategic investments, sustain buybacks, and weather cyclical softness. Strong absolute cash generation underpins capital allocation optionality and reduces refinancing risk over the medium term.

Material de-leveraging and a much larger equity base improve solvency and strategic optionality. Reduced leverage (~0.5 debt/equity TTM) lowers interest and covenant risk, enabling M&A, AV commitments, and buybacks from a position of greater financial strength over coming quarters.

Sustained >20% gross bookings growth and expanding monthly active consumers demonstrate compounding network effects. Large scale boosts unit economics, cross-sell potential (mobility+delivery), and product leverage, supporting durable revenue growth and competitive advantage in core markets.

bear.b: A multiyear ~$10B AV program and vehicle commitments tie up capital and create execution and regulatory risk. These long-duration investments can weigh on free cash flow allocation and margin conversion as commercialization remains early and returns are uncertain over the next several years.

A ~500bp decline in reported mobility take rate (largely from a U.K. model change) shows that revenue margin metrics can move materially. Persistent or recurring margin compression would limit sustainable operating margins and the ability to convert bookings growth into durable profit expansion.

Aggressive local competitors in markets like Brazil pressure volumes and require higher incentive spending to secure drivers and couriers. Elevated supply costs in key emerging markets can erode unit economics and constrain margin improvement across the global platform over the medium term.
